issues.subject: Azure US [US] deployment
issues.evidence: The public-cloud container gives only a country and no Azure Region name or official code (1 of 2 public-cloud deployments).

issues.subject: dc-cn-primary zone model
issues.evidence: Project config requires DMZ, Intranet, App Zone, and DB Zone; the PNG/blueprint contains only Intranet, App Zone, and DB Zone. F5, WAF, edge router, and SYS-04 web are placed in Intranet rather than the required DMZ web tier.

issues.subject: dc-us zone model
issues.evidence: Project config defines five NA zones; the diagram adds unapproved NA-PROD-INA-EARTH for SYS-28 through SYS-30 and provides no approved DMZ ingress zone.

issues.subject: Azure SYS-56 and SYS-57 network placement
issues.evidence: Both Azure components are inside an APP Zone but no VNET, Subnet, endpoint type, or Private Endpoint is drawn (2 of 2 Azure components).

issues.subject: AWS SYS-55 network placement
issues.evidence: A Private subnet (APP) is shown, but its containing VPC and account/network boundary are not identified (1 of 1 AWS components).

issues.subject: City C, State X [US]
issues.evidence: The same physical location is drawn as two independent private-DC containers (dc-us and dc-us-identity) instead of nested zones in one DC boundary.

issues.subject: AWS US East deployment
issues.evidence: No Hub VPC, Transit Gateway, central firewall, DNS, SIEM, or governed Spoke VPC is shown.

issues.subject: Azure US deployment
issues.evidence: No Hub VNET, Spoke VNET, firewall, Bastion, gateway, DNS, or monitoring boundary is shown.

issues.subject: seven cross-DC/cloud relationships
issues.evidence: None of the 7 cross-boundary relationships identifies MPLS/equivalent private line, AWS Direct Connect, or Azure ExpressRoute: 2 web-to-ADFS, 2 CN/NA Kafka, 1 NA/AWS, and 2 NA/Azure.

issues.subject: four cross-boundary relationships
issues.evidence: The 2 web-to-ADFS and 2 NA-to-Azure labels do not explicitly state TLS/IPSec encryption; only the Kafka cross-boundary labels include Mutual TLS.

issues.subject: CN and NA north-south ingress
issues.evidence: The Internet symbol has no arrow to SYS-01 or SYS-28. The blueprint starts at F5, so neither of the 2 intended external paths proves Internet -> F5, and both F5 stacks are outside a DMZ.

issues.subject: CN and NA ingress security boundaries
issues.evidence: The private-cloud standard requires firewalls at Internet-to-DMZ and DMZ-to-internal boundaries. Neither boundary is drawn in either region; F5 and optional in-plan WAF nodes do not document those firewall controls.

issues.subject: six direct SAP service calls
issues.evidence: SYS-06/07/09 directly call SYS-20/21 and SYS-33/34/36 directly call SYS-45 over RFC/SNC, bypassing APIH/WSO2/Kafka. The CDC chains themselves are mediated correctly through Debezium -> RabbitMQ -> Kafka.

issues.subject: SYS-17 -> SYS-54 and SYS-42 -> SYS-55
issues.evidence: Two Kafka consumer relationships point away from Kafka; the rule requires consumer arrows to point toward the Kafka node. All 103 arrows are otherwise single-direction and carry protocol/auth text in the blueprint/draw.io source.

issues.subject: AuthZ Platform
issues.evidence: The blueprint narrative names AuthZ Platform and application RBAC, but no authorization component or enforcement relationship appears in the PNG.

issues.subject: AWS SYS-55 credentials
issues.evidence: The blueprint states peer-owned KMS/Secrets Manager, but the diagram has no IAM role, Secrets Manager/KMS node, usage relationship, or rotation evidence.

issues.subject: Azure SYS-56 and SYS-57 credentials
issues.evidence: The blueprint states peer-owned Key Vault/managed identity, but the diagram has no Key Vault, Managed Identity, usage relationship, soft-delete, or purge-protection evidence.

issues.subject: three private-DC operational paths
issues.evidence: PAW, office network, management plane, MFA/JIT, and target relationships exist only as blueprint prose; no PAW node or path is drawn for dc-cn-primary, dc-us, or dc-us-identity.

issues.subject: AWS operational access
issues.evidence: No PAW, Systems Manager Session Manager, or governed administrative path is visible for the AWS deployment.

issues.subject: Azure operational access
issues.evidence: No Azure Bastion Standard, JIT control, or governed administrative path is visible for the Azure deployment.

issues.subject: two CN/NA Kafka data flows
issues.evidence: Both cross-border Kafka arrows omit data classification and an approved compliance basis. Blueprint text says legal basis is required, not that one has been approved, and the arrows do not carry the label.

issues.subject: 44 physical entities
issues.evidence: Exact draw.io inventory: 34 of 60 physical component nodes and 10 of 12 physical zone/subnet containers use dashed borders, which the standard reserves for logical concepts.

issues.subject: 47 of 60 technical components
issues.evidence: Only 13 components are visibly enclosed by the explicitly named NA-PROD-INA-K8S platform zone. Runtime values for the other 47 exist only in draw.io tooltips/blueprint fields and are absent from the exported PNG.

issues.subject: SYS-13 and SYS-40
issues.evidence: Both components are named 'etc.', a generic placeholder that cannot be mapped to a deployable service (2 of 60 components).

issues.subject: service component shapes
issues.evidence: Many backend, frontend, network, identity, and third-party service nodes use square dashed rectangles instead of rounded physical-service rectangles.

issues.subject: 103 interaction labels across 60 components
issues.evidence: Visual inspection of the PNG shows dense opaque protocol/auth labels and crossing lines covering component names, zone contents, and one another, especially in both application stacks and between CN/NA. The exported view is not reviewable at normal scale.

issues.subject: nine database/cache stores
issues.evidence: At-rest encryption is described in blueprint notes but is not visibly labeled on the nine cylinder nodes in the PNG.

issues.subject: SYS-02 and SYS-29 WAF controls
issues.evidence: Both WAFs are symmetric but marked in-plan/optional pending a security-owner decision. Resolve the control decision and depict the approved deployed state; F5 remains mandatory independently.
